title: AI Agents, Tool Use & MCP: Building Agents with Least Privilege
concept: Build agents that stay inside their lane: decide when a fixed workflow is enough, write the agent loop around a scripted fake model, design narrow tools with argument schemas, expose internal data through a Model Context Protocol server, enforce permissions, human approval, step and budget limits, treat tool output as untrusted data, and audit every call so a run can be replayed.
description: An expert course for engineers who give a model tools and must make sure it cannot do more than it should. Every lesson starts from an incident around the CodeDev learning platform's Study-Plan Agent and its operations agent - an agent used where a three-step workflow would do, a tool whose vague description made the model call it with the wrong user, a loop that ran 200 steps on a failing tool, a support ticket whose text told the agent to delete data in the wrong environment, a write tool that ran without the learner's confirmation - and fixes it in TypeScript against a scripted fake model: the agent loop, stop conditions, a tool registry with schema validation, an MCP-style tools/list and tools/call server, a permission policy with confirmation for writes, untrusted tool output, token and time budgets, and an audit log. 12 lessons, 30 evidence-based True/False statements and 9 TypeScript challenges. No real model or network is used.

lessons.title: Workflow or agent? Choosing the least autonomy that works
The agent loop: model turns, tool calls and a final answer
Stop conditions: step limits and runs that end on purpose
Designing narrow tools: names, descriptions & argument schemas
MCP: hosts, clients, servers and the JSON-RPC lifecycle
Build an MCP tool server: tools/list, tools/call & schema validation
Least privilege: read tools run, write tools ask first
Tool output is data: confused deputies and indirect injection
Token and time budgets: stopping a run before it gets expensive
Audit logs: recording every tool call so a run can be replayed
Spot the AI Mistake: the agent that never stops retrying
